newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industry output to fall but worst over - study.
newsitem.headline: Italy industry output to fall but worst over - study.

text.p: Italian manufacturing output is seen rising by just an annual 0.2 percent at end-1996 against a June forecast of a 1.9 percent rise, but the cyclical lows have now passed, an economic study said.

The report, by private research body Prometeia and Banca Commerciale Italiana's research unit, said the government's restrictive budget policies ahead of European economic and monetary union, as well as a fall in export volumes, would weigh on production.

Revising down its earlier forecast, the report said "the expected recovery for the elements of domestic demand in Italy and Europe must be postponed until 1998," due to the commitment of aspiring member nations to respect Maastricht criteria.

On the foreign trade front, the study noted that Italian industries had moved from an aggressive price strategy to sales policies aimed at safeguarding market shares, with a negative impact on export volumes.
Industrial activity levels had been on a downtrend since the second half of 1995 but the worst now seemed to be over, although recovery would be slow, it said.
Latest official data showed industrial production fell an unadjusted 11.3 percent year-on-year in August after a 4.1 percent rise in July.
The 1996-98 period was likely to be a phase of low growth with falling margins and operating costs tending slowly to accelerate," the report added.
